FIRST FLAKES: the first thin flakes of the evening beginning to fall, catching in the warm window light
STRAIGHT SMOKE: chimney smoke rising in a perfectly straight plume into the cold still air above the roofline
LAMP LIT: a lamp flickering on inside, a square of amber warmth spreading across the snow below the sill
AURORA SURGE: the aurora rippling brighter across the sky, washing the snowfield in shifting green and violet
STREAK: a shooting star crossing the dark overhead, trailing a brief bright scratch of light
OPENING DOOR: the cabin door swinging open and a flood of golden light spilling across the snow
SOFT FLURRY: the first gentle flurry of the evening drifting down through the beam of the porch lamp
STILL PLUME: smoke from the chimney climbing straight and slow into the perfectly windless night air
WINDOW GLOW: a window coming on as a lamp is lit inside, amber light pooling on the crust below
RIPPLE: the aurora rippling and brightening suddenly, its curtains folding and unfolding across the zenith
FALLING STAR: a shooting star crossing the upper sky, burning out just above the dark treeline
ROOF PLUME: a gust lifting a plume of powder off the roof ridge and carrying it glittering into the dark
RAIN EASING: the rain easing off at last, the eaves beginning to drip in a steady ticking rhythm
EARLY SNOW: the very first flakes of the evening appearing, spiralling slowly through the lamplight
SMOKE PLUME: chimney smoke rising as a clean pale plume, barely bending, dissolving high in the still air
DOOR SPILL: the front door opening wide, a warm rectangle of light reaching far out across the blue snow
BRIGHT BAND: the aurora surging into a vivid green band, its lower edge shimmering and dancing
SWIFT STREAK: a shooting star crossing fast and low, leaving a momentary silver line across the dark
EAVE DRIP: the rain softening to a murmur, the eaves beginning to shed bright drops one by one
GUST LIFT: a sudden gust lifting a curling plume of dry snow off the eaves and swirling it away
SNOWFALL STARTS: the first scattered flakes of the night beginning to fall, settling on the lit windowsill
SMOKE STILL: chimney smoke rising absolutely straight, its pale thread unwavering in the breathless air
LIT ROOM: a lamp coming on and warming a window to gold, the light trembling faintly as the flame settles
SHOWER END: the last of the rain easing away, the eaves releasing slow heavy drops into the quiet
METEOR: a shooting star crossing the high dark in a clean bright arc, fading above the far ridge
